- "content": "```typescript export interface PreloaderOptions ```
Property Modifiers Type Description
maxIdlePreloads? number _(Optional)_ Maximum number of simultaneous preload links that the preloader will maintain. If you set this higher, the browser will have all JS files in memory sooner, but it will contend with other resource downloads. Furthermore, if a bundle suddenly becomes more likely, it will have to wait longer to be preloaded. Bundles that reach 100% probability (static imports of other bundles) will always be preloaded immediately, no limit. `0` stops the preloader from starting speculative preloads in the browser. An interaction that needs code which has not loaded yet then waits for its download. The links from `ssrPreloads` are separate and still go out. Defaults to `25`
ssrPreloads? number _(Optional)_ Maximum number of preload links to add during SSR. These instruct the browser to preload likely bundles before the preloader script is active: the first ones the preloader would fetch for the page, ranked the same way by probability, so shared static imports such as core come first. Setting this to 0 will disable all preload links. Preload links can delay LCP, which is a Core Web Vital, but they can improve TTI, which is not a Core Web Vital but more noticeable to the user. Defaults to `5`: the bundles the preloader ranks first, which normally include core and the handler bundles the page's events and tasks run through.

### Buffered and on-demand modulepreloads (a.k.a. the preloader)

-To not compete with visual content loading (FCP & LCP), Qwik links only the few most likely bundles right away (`ssrPreloads`, 5 by default) and waits for the browser `load` event before streaming the rest of the javascript bundles. Once the `load` event fires, Qwik starts to buffer `<link rel="modulepreload" href="..." as="script">` tags to speculatively preload the most likely code executed by the user.

+To not compete with visual content loading (FCP & LCP), Qwik links only core and the handlers a page's events need right away, and waits for the browser `load` event before streaming the rest of the javascript bundles. Once the `load` event fires, Qwik starts to buffer `<link rel="modulepreload" href="..." as="script">` tags to speculatively preload the most likely code executed by the user.

By default a queue of idle preloads is set to a maximum of 25 simultaneous preloads through the [`maxIdlePreloads`](link). Preloads are therefore buffered in a queue of 25 until all bundles have been preloaded. If a user interaction happens during buffering, the preloader will append the corresponding bundles modulepreload link tags, bypassing the idle queue and starting to preload them right away.
